mainTopic: Is night (and שבת) a time for תפילין? רבה בר רב הונא's view, the source that excludes nights and שבתות, wearing תפילין after sunset, touching one's תפילין, and the left arm
overview: This amud asks whether night and שבת are times for wearing תפילין. The גמרא first says that רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא wore תפילין at evening prayers, so they held that night is a time for תפילין. It then shows that רבה בר רב הונא's rule about taking off תפילין at dark was said only about ערב שבת. That raises a problem: the פסוק that leaves out שבת also leaves out nights, as רבי יוסי הגלילי teaches. The answer is that רבה בר רב הונא learns the שבת exemption from רבי עקיבא's source. That source says שבת and יום טוב are already an 'אות', a sign, and it says nothing about nights. Next, רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן argue about whether wearing תפילין after sunset breaks a עשה or a לאו. They also explain how they read the word 'השמר'. רבי אלעזר permits wearing them at night to guard them, and רבינא tells how רב אשי held that night is allowed but did not rule so in public. The amud ends with two rules: a person must keep touching his תפילין, learned from the ציץ, and the תפילין של יד go on the left arm.

steps.title: Two sages wore תפילין when praying at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling quoted just before this, using the practice of רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, who prayed in the evening while wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא used to pray the evening prayer while wearing תפילין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just quoted by pointing to two great sages who wore תפילין at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling said before this held back people from wearing תפילין at night. If respected sages openly wore them at evening prayers, it seems they did not accept that ruling. A story about what sages actually did is being used as evidence against a stated rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Leather boxes with פסוקים, worn on the arm and head

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: But Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna
would pray with them in the evening?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מְצַלּוּ בְּהוּ בְּאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the passage by challenging the ruling quoted earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ruling against wearing תפילין at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leading sages actually wore תפילין at night, which goes against the ruling.

steps.title: Those sages simply held a different opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the practice of these sages reflects a different opinion that disagrees with the earlier ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: That practice follows an opinion that disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying these sages simply held a different view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to make the story fit the ruling. It admits there is a real disagreement: these sages held that night is a time for תפילין. This answer sets up the next question about רבה בר רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees; it is a different opinion

phrases.english: That one disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone agreed with the earlier ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: These sages held a different opinion: that night is a time for תפילין.

steps.title: Did רבה בר רב הונא really hold that night is a time for תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבה בר רב הונא allowed תפילין at night, citing his ruling that once it is surely dark one takes them off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבה בר רב הונא really say this? But he said: if it is unclear whether it is dark yet, one does not take off the תפילין and does not put them on. This shows that if it is surely dark, one takes them off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבה בר רב הונא himself seems to rule that one must take off תפילין once night has surely come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ruling about a doubtful case teaches something by implication: in a case of no doubt, when it is surely night, one removes the תפילין. That suggests he holds night is NOT a time for תפילין. This goes against the story in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: It is unclear whether it is already dark (night)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not what רבה בר רב הונא says outright. It comes from the implication (הא) of his words: since he only says not to remove them in a case of doubt, it follows that when it is surely dark, one does remove them.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי?
phrases.english: And did Rabba bar Rav Huna say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar Rav Huna say:
If it is uncertain whether it is dark or not dark –
phrases.notes: Some versions say לָא, in the round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, says אֵין. Both mean "not."

phrases.english: he neither takes them off nor puts them on,
this implies that if it is surely dark – he takes them off!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind step 2, that רבה בר רב הונא holds night is a time for תפילין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבה בר רב הונא allows תפילין at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own ruling implies that one must take off תפילין once it is surely night, which contradicts what he did.

steps.title: That ruling was said about ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ruling about taking off תפילין at dark was said only about Friday evening, when שבת is starting.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling was said about ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבה בר רב הונא's rule about removing תפילין at dark applies only on Friday evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason to take them off at dark is not that night has come. It is that שבת has come, and תפילין are not worn on שבת. So on a regular weeknight, he could still hold that night is a time for תפילין.

phrases.english: There, it was said about Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His ruling was about every night, so night is not a time for תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: His ruling was only about Friday night, because שבת is not a time for תפילין.

steps.title: Nights and שבת stand or fall together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: you cannot split night from שבת, because the same source that leaves out שבת also leaves out nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold? If he holds that night is a time for תפילין, then שבת is also a time for תפילין. If he holds that שבת is not a time for תפילין, then night is also not a time for תפילין. This is because nights are left out from the very same place that leaves out שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 4 by showing that night and שבת must go together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 needed רבה בר רב הונא to hold two things: night IS a time for תפילין, but שבת is NOT. The גמרא says both rules come from one source, so you cannot accept one and reject the other. That leaves his position looking impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion
A time when the מצוה of תפילין applies
Is excluded (from a rule, based on a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the important idea that the exclusion of nights and the exclusion of שבת come from one shared source, so a sage's view on one usually decides his view on the other.

phrases.english: What does he hold?
If he holds night is a time for tefillin,
Shabbat is also a time for tefillin.

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר שַׁבָּת לָאו זְמַן תְּפִילִּין,
phrases.english: If he holds Shabbat is not a time for tefillin,
night is also not a time for tefillin,
because from the place where Shabbat is excluded
from there nights are excluded.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר לַיְלָה זְמַן תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבה בר רב הונא's ruling applies only to ערב שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nights and שבת are left out by the same source, so one cannot hold night is a time for תפילין while holding שבת is not.

steps.title: The פסוק that leaves out both nights and שבתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that nights and שבת come from one source, quoting a ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי learns both exclusions from one פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: "And you shall keep this law in its season, from days to days" – "days," and not nights. "From days" – and not all days, which leaves out שבתות and ימים טובים. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind step 5: one פסוק teaches both that תפילין are not worn at night and not worn on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ימים ("days") leaves out nights. The extra letter מ in מימים ("from days") means "some days but not all," which leaves out שבתות and ימים טובים. Since both rules come from one פסוק, whoever accepts this reading must accept both.

keyTerms.meaning: "From days to days," meaning from year to year

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"And you shall keep this law
in its season from days to days" –
phrases.notes: שמות 13:10. This פסוק comes at the end of the section about פסח and תפילין.

phrases.english: "days" and not nights,
"from days" and not all days,
phrases.notes: The extra letter מ, meaning "from," is read as "only some of the days."

phrases.english: excluding Shabbatot and Festivals,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that nights and שבת are left out from one source
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading שמות 13:10 according to רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: this פסוק is only about פסח
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי עקיבא disagrees and says the פסוק is only about the קרבן פסח, not about תפילין at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: this law was said only about פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי עקיבא's opposing view: the פסוק has nothing to do with תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, this פסוק teaches nothing about when תפילין are worn. So it does not leave out nights or שבת for תפילין. The shared source from step 6 belongs only to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, one פסוק (שמות 13:10) teaches that תפילין are not worn at night and not on שבתות and ימים טובים, so the two rules go together. רבי עקיבא says that פסוק is only about the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
this law was not stated
except for the Paschal offering alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק "ושמרת את החקה הזאת" refers only to the קרבן פסח, not to תפילין.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא learns the שבת exemption from a different source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5. רבה בר רב הונא learns that שבת is exempt from תפילין from רבי עקיבא's source, not from the פסוק that also leaves out nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the same place רבי עקיבא learns it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 5. רבה בר רב הונא does not learn the שבת exemption from רבי יוסי הגלילי's פסוק. He learns it from a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said that nights and שבת come out of one פסוק, so you cannot accept one and reject the other. The answer is that רבה בר רב הונא takes the שבת exemption from רבי עקיבא's source instead. That leaves him free to say that nights are not excluded at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (he learns it from)

phrases.english: He derives it from the place
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבה בר רב הונא, and 'it' is the rule that there are no תפילין on שבת.

phrases.english: from which Rabbi Akiva derives it,

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהֵיכָא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא from step 7 to answer the קשיא of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source for the same law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שבת exemption must come from the same פסוק that also excludes nights
steps.terutzMaskana: The שבת exemption comes from רבי עקיבא's 'אות' source, so nights are not excluded

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source: שבת and יום טוב are themselves a sign
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows רבי עקיבא learning from the word 'אות' that תפילין are not worn on שבת and יום טוב. Those days are already a sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: You might think a person should put on תפילין on שבת and יום טוב. So the פסוק says: 'It shall be a sign on your hand and a reminder between your eyes.' תפילין are for days that need a sign. That leaves out שבת and יום טוב, which are a sign by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows what רבי עקיבא's source is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are called an 'אות', a sign of the bond between ה׳ and the Jewish people. שבת and יום טוב are already such a sign, so a second sign is not needed. This source says nothing about nights, so it fits רבה בר רב הונא, who allows תפילין at night.

keyTerms.meaning: Head תפילין (a reminder between the eyes)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's 'אות' reasoning leaves out שבת and יום טוב but not nights. That is how רבה בר רב הונא can allow תפילין at night.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
One might think a person should put on tefillin
on Shabbatot and Yamim Tovim?
The verse teaches:
"And it shall be for a sign on your hand
and for a reminder between your eyes" —
those days that need a sign,
this leaves out Shabbatot and Yamim Tovim
which are themselves a sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא behind the answer in step 8
steps.raayaObject: That the שבת exemption can come from a source that does not exclude nights
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי עקיבא on 'והיה לאות'

steps.title: Wearing תפילין after sunset: breaking a עשה or a לאו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that someone who puts on תפילין after sunset breaks a positive command. רבי יוחנן says he breaks a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Anyone who puts on תפילין after sunset breaks a positive command. רבי יוחנן said: He breaks a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement. Both אמוראים hold that תפילין may not be worn after sunset. They argue about what kind of sin it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them follow the view that nights are excluded, which is learned from 'ושמרת את החקה הזאת' (step 6). Their argument is about that פסוק: does it make a positive command (עשה) or a prohibition (לאו)?
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think either of them allows תפילין at night. Both forbid it. They only argue about whether the sin is a עשה or a לאו.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Anyone who puts on tefillin
after sunset
violates a positive מצוה,
and Rabbi Yochanan says:
he violates a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל הַמַּנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין אַחַר שְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related discussion about תפילין at night
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: after sunset it breaks a עשה. רבי יוחנן: it breaks a לאו.

steps.title: Suggesting they argue about רבי אבין's rule on 'השמר'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the dispute depends on רבי אבין's rule. That rule says the words 'השמר', 'פן' and 'אל' always mean a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about what רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא? רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא: Every place the Torah says 'השמר' (be careful), 'פן' (lest) or 'אל' (do not), it is only a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason for the argument between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן. The next line will spell it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night exclusion comes from 'ושמרת', which comes from the same root as 'השמר'. If that word always makes a לאו, then wearing תפילין at night breaks a לאו. So the dispute might depend on whether you accept this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)
'Be careful', 'lest', 'do not': warning words in the Torah

phrases.english: Shall we say that about Rabbi Avin's statement
in the name of Rabbi Ile'a they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Avin said in the name of Rabbi Ile'a:
Every place where it says
"be careful," "lest," or "do not,"
it is nothing but a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בְּרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the reason behind the dispute in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute about whether רבי אבין's rule is accepted?

steps.title: Spelling out the suggestion
steps.stepSummary: One sage, רבי יוחנן, accepts רבי אבין's rule, so he says לאו. The other sage, רבי אלעזר, does not accept it, so he says עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One sage holds like רבי אבין, and the other sage does not hold like רבי אבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion by matching each sage to a side of רבי אבין's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן accepts the rule, so 'ושמרת' makes a לאו. רבי אלעזר rejects it, so 'ושמרת' stays a positive command. The suggestion would mean that רבי אלעזר disagrees with a widely used rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold this view

phrases.english: For one Sage holds like Rabbi Avin,
phrases.notes: That's רבי יוחנן, who says it's a לאו.

phrases.english: and the other Sage does not hold like Rabbi Avin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggestion begun in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggestion: רבי יוחנן accepts רבי אבין's rule and רבי אלעזר rejects it

steps.title: Both accept רבי אבין's rule but argue about 'השמר' written on a positive command
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone accepts רבי אבין's rule. They argue only about 'השמר' that is written about a positive command.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone accepts what רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא. Here they argue about this point. One sage holds: 'השמר' written about a prohibition is a prohibition, and 'השמר' written about a positive command is a positive command. The other sage holds: 'השמר' written about a positive command is also a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion and gives a smaller, sharper reason for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that 'השמר' takes on the type of the מצוה it is attached to. Since תפילין is a positive command, 'ושמרת' there makes a עשה. רבי יוחנן holds that 'השמר' always makes a לאו, even when it is attached to a positive command.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Be careful' written about a positive command

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: 'השמר' on a positive command makes a עשה. רבי יוחנן: 'השמר' always makes a לאו. Both accept רבי אבין's rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for reading the Torah's warning words. The same word 'השמר' can either add a separate prohibition or just strengthen a positive command.

phrases.english: No, everyone holds
like Rabbi Avin in the name of Rabbi Ile'a,
and here they disagree about this:
One Sage holds: "be careful" about a prohibition is a prohibition,
phrases.notes: This first sage is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: and "be careful" about a positive מצוה is a positive מצוה,
and the other Sage holds: "be careful" about a positive מצוה is also a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in steps 11 and 12 and gives a new explanation
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects that the dispute is about accepting רבי אבין's rule at all
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion wrongly makes רבי אלעזר reject a rule he actually accepts. The real argument is narrower: 'השמר' written about a positive command.

steps.title: Wearing תפילין at night to keep them safe is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that putting on תפילין after dark is permitted if the reason is to guard them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: if a person puts them on at night to keep them safe, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives an exception to his own earlier rule against wearing תפילין after sunset. If the goal is only to protect the תפילין, it is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבי אלעזר said that wearing תפילין after sunset breaks an עשה. Here he explains that this applies only when the person wears them for the מצוה. If he wears them just so they won't be stolen or lost, there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: to guard them, to keep them safe

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
And if it is to guard them, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: He means putting on תפילין after dark only so they stay safe, for example from theft.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: וְאִם לְשׇׁמְרָן – מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to רבי אלעזר's ban on wearing תפילין after sunset.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wearing תפילין at night only to guard them is permitted.

steps.title: רבינא sees רב אשי put on תפילין after dark
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells how רב אשי put on תפילין after dark and said it was to guard them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: I was sitting in front of רב אשי, it got dark, and he put on תפילין. I asked him: Do you need them to keep them safe? He told me: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tells a story about his teacher רב אשי putting on תפילין after nightfall. רב אשי says he did it to guard them, which fits רבי אלעזר's exception. This story sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, the story is a case of the 'to guard them' exception from step 14. But רבינא is preparing to tell us what he thought רב אשי's real reason was.

phrases.english: And Ravina said:
I was sitting before Rav Ashi
and it grew dark, and he put on tefillin.
And I said to him:
Does the Master need them in order to guard them?
And he said to me: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבִינָא: הֲוָה יָתֵיבְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life case that seems to use רבי אלעזר's 'to guard them' exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי put on תפילין after dark and said it was to guard them.

steps.title: רב אשי's real view: it is the הלכה, but not taught publicly
steps.stepSummary: רבינא saw that רב אשי did not really mean 'to guard them.' He held that night is a time for תפילין, but this is not taught to the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I could see in his mind that he did not really need them to guard them. He holds: this is the halacha, but we do not teach it that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains what רב אשי really thought. רב אשי holds that one may wear תפילין at night, but he does not rule this way openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא understood that the answer 'yes, to guard them' was not רב אשי's real reason. רב אשי's own view is that night is a proper time for תפילין, unlike רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן. Since this is not given out as a public ruling, he gave a reason that everyone would accept.

keyTerms.meaning: it is the halacha, but we do not give a public ruling that way
his real intention, what was in his mind
he holds, this is his view

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי did not lie about the הלכה. He really holds that wearing תפילין at night is allowed. He just does not teach it in public, so he gave the safe reason of 'guarding them.'
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר allows תפילין at night only to guard them. רב אשי holds that night is truly allowed, but that we do not rule this way publicly.

phrases.english: But I saw his intention
that it was not to guard them that he needed them.
He holds: it is the halacha, but we do not rule that way.
phrases.notes: The הלכה here is that night is also a proper time for תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲזֵיתֵיהּ לְדַעְתֵּיהּ דְּלָאו לְשׇׁמְרָן הוּא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the true reason behind רב אשי's action in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב אשי (as רבינא understood him), night is a proper time for תפילין by the הלכה, but this is not given out as a public ruling.

steps.title: A person must keep touching his תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that a person must touch his תפילין regularly the whole time he wears them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: a person must touch his תפילין at all times.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule about wearing תפילין is given: you must keep feeling them now and then so you remember you have them on. The next step brings the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a person should not forget that he is wearing תפילין. Touching them often keeps his mind on them.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
A person is obligated to touch his tefillin
at all times,
phrases.notes: He means all the time he is wearing them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בַּתְּפִילִּין בְּכׇל שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new rule about how to wear תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must touch his תפילין regularly while wearing them.

steps.title: Proof from the ציץ of the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned through a קל וחומר: the ציץ has one name of ה׳ and must never be forgotten, so תפילין, with many names, surely must not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a קל וחומר from the ציץ. The ציץ has only one mention of ה׳'s name, and the Torah says: 'It shall be on his forehead always,' meaning he must not take his mind off it. תפילין have many mentions of ה׳'s name, so all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא proves his rule with a קל וחומר from the ציץ, the golden plate on the כהן גדול's forehead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תמיד' teaches that the כהן גדול must always be aware of the ציץ. The ציץ has ה׳'s name only once, while the פרשיות in the תפילין have it many times. So if one name requires constant awareness, many names require it even more, and touching the תפילין keeps that awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'how much more so' argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
the golden plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead
take his mind off, become distracted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the duty to touch the תפילין regularly the whole time they are worn, so that one never forgets them.

phrases.english: This is learned by a kal vachomer from the frontplate.
And if the frontplate, which has on it
only one mention of God's name,
the Torah said about it:
"And it shall be on his forehead always,"
meaning that he should not take his mind off it,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording is in square brackets. Either way, it means the same thing.

phrases.english: then tefillin, which have many mentions of God's name,
how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The duty to touch and stay aware of one's תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from 'והיה על מצחו תמיד' said about the ציץ.

steps.title: 'Your hand' means the left arm
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'ידך' in the תפילין פסוק means the left arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Your hand' means the left.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא says that the תפילין של יד go on the left arm, since that is what 'ידך' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'on your hand' without saying which one. The ברייתא states that this means the left arm, and the next steps will challenge and then prove it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Your hand" – this is the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: which arm gets the תפילין של יד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תפילין של יד are put on the left arm.

steps.title: Maybe it means the right arm?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know it is the left arm and not the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is the left, or maybe it is only the right?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the question of why 'ידך' should not mean the right arm. This sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a plain 'hand' means the main hand, the right one. The ברייתא asks this so it can show from the language of the פסוקים that 'יד' alone means the left.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps it is only (a standard way to raise the other possibility)

phrases.english: Do you say it is the left,
or perhaps it is only the right?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שְׂמֹאל, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ruling of step 19 so that it can be proven.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that 'ידך' means left and not right?

steps.title: Three פסוקים where 'יד' is the left and 'ימין' is the right
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings three פסוקים in which 'יד' and 'ימין' appear side by side. This shows that plain 'יד' means the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Even My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens.' Another says: 'Her hand she put to the tent peg, and her right hand to the workmen's hammer.' Another says: 'Why do You pull back Your hand and Your right hand? Draw it out of Your bosom and destroy them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question with three פסוקים from נביאים and כתובים. In each one, 'יד' and 'ימין' are named as two different hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ימין' is used for the right hand, then the 'יד' mentioned next to it must be the other hand, the left. This shows that when the Torah just says 'ידך,' it means the left arm. Three separate פסוקים are brought to show that this is a steady pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: and it also says (brings another פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The תפילין של יד go on the left arm, because in תנ"ך, 'יד' alone is used for the left hand while the right hand is called 'ימין.'

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Even My hand founded the earth,
and My right hand spread out the heavens,"
And it says:
"Her hand she put to the tent peg,
and her right hand to the workmen's hammer,"
And it says:
"Why do You pull back Your hand, even Your right hand?
Draw it out of Your bosom and destroy them."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אַף יָדִי יָסְדָה אֶרֶץ וִימִינִי טִפְּחָה שָׁמָיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 with proof-texts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 48:13, שופטים 5:26, and תהלים 74:11, where 'יד' and 'ימין' are named as two different hands.
